hints: Write $y = 2 + 3(2x-1)^{-1}$ and apply the chain rule.
walkthrough:
Express $y$ in index form as $y = 2 + 3(2x - 1)^{-1}$ and differentiate using the chain rule:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 3(-1)(2x - 1)^{-2} \times 2$$

hints: Consider whether the fraction $-\frac{6}{(2x-1)^2}$ can ever equal zero.
walkthrough:
Set $\frac{dy}{dx} = 0$ to test for stationary points:
$$-\frac{6}{(2x - 1)^2} = 0 \implies -6 = 0$$

Explain why this equation has no solutions:
$$\text{Since the numerator is a non-zero constant } (-6)\text{, } \frac{dy}{dx} \ne 0 \text{ for all } x \ne \frac{1}{2}\text{, so the curve has no stationary points.}$$

hints: Find the coordinates of $P(2, 3)$ and evaluate $\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{2}{3}$.
Form the normal line equation $y - 3 = \frac{3}{2}(x - 2)$ and show it has $y$-intercept $0$.
walkthrough:
Evaluate the $y$-coordinate and derivative at $x = 2$:
$$y = 2 + \frac{3}{2(2) - 1} = 2 + 1 = 3 \implies P(2, 3)$$
$$\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=2} = -\frac{6}{(2(2) - 1)^2} = -\frac{6}{3^2} = -\frac{2}{3}$$

Determine the gradient of the normal to the curve at $P$:
$$m_{\text{normal}} = -\frac{1}{-\frac{2}{3}} = \frac{3}{2}$$

Form the equation of the normal line passing through $P(2, 3)$:
$$y - 3 = \frac{3}{2}(x - 2) \implies y - 3 = \frac{3}{2}x - 3 \implies y = \frac{3}{2}x$$

Verify that the normal passes through the origin $(0, 0)$:
$$\text{When } x = 0:\quad y = \frac{3}{2}(0) = 0$$
$$\text{Thus the normal passes through } (0, 0)$$

State the connected rates of change relation:
$$\frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{dy}{dx} \times \frac{dx}{dt}$$

Calculate the rate of change of $y$:
$$\frac{dy}{dt} = 0.04\text{ units per second}$$
